RT01.name: Data model, schema and identity design

RT02.name: Data sources and ingestion setup
RT02.scope: Connect the agreed sources such as CRM, loyalty, commerce and web or app events, map fields to XDM, enable datasets for Profile and check that the first loads build the expected profiles.
RT02.evidence: You can ingest data from a variety of sources such as Adobe applications, cloud-based storages, databases, and many others.

RT03.name: Profile and merge policy configuration
RT03.scope: Set the merge method and dataset priority in the default merge policy, review how the identity graph links records, and check sample profiles against source data.
RT03.evidence: merge policies are the rules that Experience Platform uses to determine how data will be prioritized

RT04.name: Audience build and destination activation
RT04.scope: Build the starting audiences, connect the agreed destinations, choose the identities and attributes to send, then schedule and test the first activations.
RT04.evidence: After you configure your destination, you can activate audiences in multiple ways

RT05.name: Governance, access and sandbox setup
RT05.scope: Set up roles, permissions and development and production sandboxes, apply data usage labels and policies to datasets, and confirm activations respect those policies.
RT05.evidence: assist your team with the right permissions, access controls, and sandbox configurations

RT06.name: Monthly audience and dataflow operations
RT06.src: Adobe Experience Platform end-to-end example workflow

JO06.name: Monthly journey operations and optimization

AXD12.name: DAM metadata ready for Coworker search
AXD12.src: Experience League: Content Discovery Agentic Capabilities Overview
AXD12.scope: Index the custom metadata properties teams search by, such as campaign, brand or license, and test discovery prompts with each team.
AXD12.evidence: To improve discovery performance, index relevant custom metadata properties.

AXE01.name: Workfront extension in the Universal Editor
AXE01.src: Experience League: Workfront + AEM Sites (One Adobe tutorial)
AXE01.scope: Where Adobe has turned on the Early Access plugin, enable the Workfront extension for the Universal Editor in Extension Manager with the client's Workfront instance and the preview and publish URL options, build the two Workfront task custom forms it uses (content fragment and integration ID, preview and publish URLs), then test it with one content review.

AXE02.name: Fusion scenarios on AEM pages
AXE02.src: Experience League: Adobe Experience Manager MCP modules (Workfront Fusion)
AXE02.scope: Where the client has Workfront Fusion, connect the Adobe Experience Manager MCP connector with a service account, limit its read-only and write or delete tools, and build scenarios that act on AEM pages from Workfront work, such as reading a page's content into a task or publishing an approved page, with a person checking each change before it goes live.
AXE02.evidence: across areas like sites, digital assets, content fragments, folders, the content repository, and content AI

AXE03.name: AEM Sites knowledge source through Content AI
AXE03.src: Experience League: Create and manage knowledge sources for Brand Concierge
AXE03.scope: In Cloud Manager, set up the Content AI source on the AEM as a Cloud Service environment (make the existing pages index searchable after checking it holds only public content, or crawl the site with exclusions and a refresh schedule), confirm it is Available with test searches, then build the AEM Sites knowledge source in Composer and attach Content AI Search to the Site Advisory skill.
AXE03.evidence: Select an existing Content AI index from the list. The list is populated from the AEM Sites as a Cloud Service instance.

XA01.name: Triggered and batch messages on CDP data
XA01.scope: Set up the client's first event-triggered messages (such as cart, browse or welcome) and scheduled sends that read Real-Time CDP audiences and profile attributes, then test entry, conditions and suppression.
XA01.evidence: Listen for a real-time behavioral or system event, then deliver a contextual message to the triggering profile

XA02.name: Multi-step journeys on CDP audiences
XA02.src: Experience League: Multi-step orchestrated journey pattern
XA02.scope: Design and build branching, multi-touch journeys that enter from Real-Time CDP audiences or events, with waits, conditions, exit criteria and decision points where the journey picks the channel or content.
XA02.evidence: Guide a profile through a branching, multi-touch journey with waits, conditions, and multiple message actions over time.

XA03.name: Journey Optimizer Decisioning and recommendations
XA03.scope: Build the offer catalog, eligibility rules, ranking strategies and placements in Journey Optimizer Decisioning on Real-Time CDP audiences and attributes, plus behavioral recommendation strategies where the catalog is large.
XA03.evidence: Use centralized decision logic to select the next-best offer or content for a profile across channels.

XA04.name: Web and app personalization on profiles
XA04.src: Experience League: Known-visitor web/app personalization pattern
XA04.scope: Configure web and app surfaces, edge audiences and content variants so known visitors see content from their profile and anonymous visitors see content from in-session behavior.
XA04.evidence: Deliver personalized content, offers, or promotions to an identified visitor based on real-time profile and segment membership

XA05.name: Share CDP audiences and attributes to Target
XA05.scope: Configure the Adobe Target destination and its workspace, choose the audiences and profile attributes to share, and check that they appear in Target for the first activities.
XA05.evidence: share audiences and profile attributes to the Adobe Target connection

XA06.name: Edge segmentation for same-page Target
XA06.scope: Set up the datastream with Target and Experience Platform services and edge segmentation, so audiences qualify in real time for same-page and next-page personalization.
XA06.evidence: Edge segmentation works as expected. Same-page and next-page personalization are supported.

XA07.name: Journey Optimizer offers in Target tests (Legacy offer decisions)
XA07.scope: Confirm Target runs on the Web SDK, then place Journey Optimizer offer decisions in manual A/B Test or Experience Targeting activities and set up the lift and conversion goals.
XA07.evidence: Adobe Target Standard or Adobe Target Premium implemented using the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK

XA08.name: Conversation signals into profiles
XA08.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge conversational experience pattern
XA08.scope: With the client's own Experience Platform license (Brand Concierge's license limits its datastream and dataset to Brand Concierge use), set up the concierge datastream and the schema fields for the conversation events Adobe documents (clicks, form submissions, booked meetings and live chats), then build the first audiences from them for activation.
XA08.evidence: feeds conversational signals back into the customer data platform for downstream personalization and activation

XA09.name: Real-Time CDP context in conversations
XA09.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge current release notes
XA09.scope: Once Adobe confirms in writing that the Limited Availability Real-Time CDP integration is enabled for this tenant, use case and region, choose the profile attributes and signals the concierge may use and test the replies against them.
XA09.evidence: incorporating Real-Time CDP context, such as user attributes, behavioral signals, and prior interactions

XA10.name: Conversation-to-purchase analysis in the client's CJA (separate license)
XA10.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge conversational experience pattern
XA10.scope: With a separately licensed CJA and Adobe's confirmation that the concierge dataset can be used there, extend the built-in dashboard with Workspace reports on conversation-to-purchase journeys, recommendation acceptance and handoff rates from the pattern's KPI list.

XA11.name: Brand Concierge block on Edge Delivery
XA11.src: Experience League: Deploy a Brand Concierge
XA11.scope: Build a block that loads the Brand Concierge script (Adobe documents the script in page code or a tag manager; the block is the partner's implementation pattern), place it on the agreed pages and navigation, and set the surface rules for where the concierge appears.
XA11.evidence: In order for Brand Concierge to appear on your website, you need to create a new custom block

XA12.name: Site content as concierge knowledge source
XA12.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge knowledge sources
XA12.scope: Set up a Website Links crawl of the Edge Delivery sitemap or URL list (the AEM Sites source applies only where the site is authored in AEM Sites with Content AI), check coverage of priority pages, and schedule refreshes.
XA12.evidence: set up knowledge source ingestion directly in Composer, with AEM website content as the primary knowledge source

XA13.name: Connect Commerce catalog to Brand Concierge
XA13.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge frequently asked questions
XA13.scope: Turn on the Commerce catalog integration (the Commerce MCP needs Live Search, an environment ID and an API key), confirm the Live Search attributes and facets the concierge needs are searchable and filterable, test product cards and comparisons, and handle custom catalog variations that need backend work. Cart, checkout and order history stay out until Adobe marks them available.
XA13.evidence: more complex or custom variations may need additional backend work

XA14.name: Commerce Data Connection to Platform
XA14.src: Experience League: Connect Commerce data to Adobe Experience Platform
XA14.scope: Configure the Commerce Services connector and Data Connection, create the schema, datasets and datastream, turn on storefront, back office and profile data, and check the first events. For an Edge Delivery storefront, send storefront events through its Experience Platform settings (XA20) and confirm how back office and profile data flow for the deployment.
XA14.evidence: you must configure both connectors, starting with the Commerce Services connector then finishing with the Data Connection extension

XA15.name: Activate CDP audiences in Commerce
XA15.scope: For Commerce on Cloud or on-premises with Real-Time CDP Prime or Ultimate, set up the Adobe Commerce destination and Audience Activation, then use the first audiences in cart price rules, dynamic blocks or related product rules.
XA15.evidence: lets you activate Real-Time CDP audiences in Adobe Commerce to create unique offers in the cart

XA16.name: Commerce event journeys, such as cart
XA16.src: Experience League: Use Journey Optimizer to send an abandoned cart email
XA16.scope: Set up the Commerce events as journey events, then build and test abandoned cart and browse journeys that read the cart and order data.
XA16.evidence: Learn how to deliver a personalized re-engagement email or notification if a cart or browser session has been abandoned.

XA17.name: Commerce data in CJA reports
XA17.scope: Add the Commerce event and profile datasets to the CJA connection, define commerce metrics and dimensions in the data view, and build the first purchase and cart reports (partner-built reports on a standard CJA connection and data view).
XA17.evidence: Customer Journey Analytics and Adobe Analytics: Gain insights into the customer and the business.

XA18.name: Build the Commerce storefront on Edge
XA18.src: Experience League: Create a storefront (Commerce Storefront)
XA18.scope: For Commerce as a Cloud Service or Commerce Optimizer, create the storefront project, link it to Commerce data, set up the drop-ins and commerce blocks, and style them to the brand.
XA18.evidence: Create a new storefront project with its own GitHub repository, Commerce connection, and starter content in Document Authoring on DA.live.

XA19.name: Storefront SEO and launch checklist
XA19.src: Experience League: Commerce Storefront launch checklist
XA19.scope: Align catalog URLs, metadata, sitemaps and prerendering with Edge Delivery defaults, then work through the storefront launch checklist and go-live plan.
XA19.evidence: Complete these steps before production traffic reaches your Adobe Commerce Storefront (EDS).

XA20.name: Storefront events to Experience Platform
XA20.src: Experience League: Commerce Storefront and Adobe Experience Platform
XA20.scope: Add the organization and datastream to the storefront configuration connect the merchant's consent management platform (the boilerplate denies consent by default), and check that product, cart and purchase events reach the Edge Network.
XA20.evidence: send commerce events (product views, purchases, cart actions) directly to the Experience Platform Edge Network

XA21.name: Target tests on Commerce shopping data
XA21.src: Experience League: Create compelling, personalized experiences at scale (Commerce)
XA21.scope: Map the Commerce events Target will use, then build the first tests on product, promotion or navigation content in the store.
XA21.evidence: Adobe Target: Test and optimize content, recommended products, offers, navigation, and more.

XA22.name: Target personalization on Edge Delivery
XA22.src: aem.live: Configuring Adobe Experience Cloud Integration
XA22.scope: Set up Target on the agreed pages through Web SDK (aem.live's recommended route), or the martech plugin where the client has it through co-innovation, with the datastream and the consent platform, and check flicker and page speed.
XA22.evidence: Datastream in the Adobe Experience Platform to connect to your Adobe Target and Adobe Analytics solutions

XA23.name: Journey Optimizer web campaigns on Edge
XA23.src: aem.live: Configuring Adobe Experience Cloud Integration
XA23.scope: Configure the martech plugin and datastream for Journey Optimizer (the datastream option, an Active-On-Edge merge policy, the Visual Editing Helper and a check of the engageable profile count), set up the web surfaces, and launch and test the first web campaigns.
XA23.evidence: Adobe Target and Adobe Journey Optimizer: personalizes and optimizes the page with your desired marketing campaigns

XA24.name: Edge Delivery site events into profiles
XA24.src: Experience League: AEM Edge Delivery Services MarTech plugin (One Adobe tutorial)
XA24.scope: Map site events to the XDM schema and datastream through the martech plugin, connect the client's consent platform (not the lab's default of consent in), then check that visits build profiles under the agreed identities.
XA24.evidence: View customer profile in Adobe Experience Platform

XA25.name: Partner-written Coworker Skills for audience work
XA25.scope: Write and test Skills for the client's own audience conventions and checks, on top of Adobe's shipped audience skills (creation, sizing, search and publish), with approval steps.
XA25.evidence: create and optimize audiences, analyze customer journeys, and uncover insights faster

XA26.name: Partner-written Coworker Skills for journey work
XA26.src: Experience League Live: Audience and Journey B2C capabilities in Coworker
XA26.scope: Write and test Skills for the client's own journey conventions and pre-launch checks, on top of Adobe's shipped journey skills (Journey Create, fallout, conflict and anomaly checks), with approval steps.
XA26.evidence: Discover how to streamline audience and journey creation and analysis.

XA27.name: Partner-written Coworker Skills for Target testing
XA27.src: Experience League: Accelerate experimentation with Coworker
XA27.scope: Write and test Skills for the client's routine Target work in its own formats, such as test briefs and results summaries, on top of Adobe's shipped Target skills (guided activity setup), with approval steps.
XA27.evidence: Skills are reusable playbooks that help Adobe CX Coworker perform customer experience orchestration tasks consistently and efficiently.

XB01.name: Campaign intake to Marketo program build
XB01.src: Experience League: Marketo & Workfront Intake and Create
XB01.scope: Build the Workfront campaign request form and the Fusion scenario that picks the right Marketo program template, clones it and passes request details into its My Tokens.
XB01.evidence: take information from the Workfront request and lookup the correct program templates

XB02.name: Email proofing and approval loop
XB02.src: Experience League: Marketo & Workfront Review and Approve
XB02.scope: Add a Ready for Review task to the project template, set up the Fusion scenario that turns the Marketo email into a Workfront proof, and send the approval back to Marketo Engage.
XB02.evidence: Approve the Workfront Proof to trigger asset approval in Marketo Engage, then mark the task as complete.

XB03.name: Program templates and tokens for automation
XB03.src: Experience League: Marketo & Workfront Intake and Create
XB03.scope: Standardize the Marketo programs and program templates the automation clones, with the My Tokens the request fills, and agree the review steps and approvers.
XB03.evidence: you will need to build out your Programs and Program Templates in Marketo Engage to utilize My Tokens

XB04.name: Marketo source connector into Platform
XB04.src: Experience League: Marketo Engage source connector overview
XB04.scope: Set up Adobe organization mapping, get the Marketo API credentials, generate the B2B namespaces and schemas, map Marketo fields to XDM and enable the people and activity datasets for Profile.
XB04.evidence: With the Marketo Engage source connector, you can bring B2B data from Marketo Engage to Experience Platform.

XB05.name: Real-Time CDP audiences to Marketo lists
XB05.src: Experience League: Marketo Engage connection destination
XB05.scope: Connect the Marketo Engage connection destination (the V2 card is Legacy), set the deduplication field (ECID is not supported) and map first name, last name and email so leads can be created, and activate the agreed audiences to Marketo static lists for nurture programs.
XB05.evidence: push audiences created in Adobe Experience Platform to Marketo where they will appear as static lists

XB06.name: Marketo Engage action in journeys
XB06.src: Experience League: Integrate with Marketo Engage (Journey Optimizer)
XB06.scope: Check the prerequisites (IMS-enabled Marketo instance in the same organization, MktoSync ingestion access), create the Marketo Engage custom action with its request payload, and add it to the agreed journeys.
XB06.evidence: A specific custom action is available in your journeys to integrate Adobe Journey Optimizer and Marketo Engage.

XB07.name: Marketo data in CJA reporting
XB07.src: Experience League: Report on Marketo Engage data
XB07.scope: Choose the ID strategy that stitches Marketo and web data, map Marketo persons and activities to XDM, ingest them, add the datasets to a CJA connection and data view, and build the first Workspace project.
XB07.evidence: Use the Marketo Engage connector to bring data from Marketo to Experience Platform.

XB08.name: Share Marketo lists with Target
XB08.src: Experience League: Send a List to Adobe Experience Cloud
XB08.scope: Set up Adobe organization mapping, send the agreed Marketo lists to Experience Cloud as synced lists, turn on access in Target, and use them in the first personalization activities.
XB08.evidence: Share Marketo list membership with Experience Platform or other solutions.

XB09.name: Site forms that submit to Marketo
XB09.src: Experience League: Submit actions for Edge Delivery Services forms
XB09.scope: Build the lead forms in Universal Editor, configure the Submit to Marketo Engage action with field mapping to Marketo, and test that submissions create or update leads.
XB09.ext: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service

XB10.name: Coworker access and skills rollout in Marketo
XB10.src: Experience League: Coworker for Marketo Engage overview
XB10.scope: Confirm Coworker is enabled for the subscription (Adobe's pages differ on its rollout) and the Gen-AI terms are accepted, set up user access and the role limits on lead investigation, and pilot the build and validate program skills on the client's own templates.
XB10.evidence: you must perform some setup steps to ensure the desired users have access

XB11.name: Brand Concierge activity in Marketo programs
XB11.src: Experience League: Brand Concierge integration with Marketo
XB11.scope: Turn on the Brand Concierge flow into Marketo, check that engagement activities and leads from forms, meetings and live chats arrive (meetings and chat need Adobe Marketo Qualifier), and build the Smart Campaigns that score, route and nurture them.
XB11.evidence: flowing every visitor interaction into Marketo as native activity data

XB13.name: Site form requests into Workfront
XB13.src: Experience League: Submit actions for Edge Delivery Services forms
XB13.scope: Configure an Edge Delivery form with the Invoke Workfront Fusion action and build the scenario that turns each submission into a Workfront request or project.
XB13.ext: AEM Forms as a Cloud Service and Workfront Fusion

XB14.name: Coworker rollout and write access
XB14.src: Experience League: Use CX Coworker in Workfront
XB14.scope: Review permissions, decide with the governance board when to turn on write access, write a starter prompt library for the client's processes and pilot it with one team.
XB14.evidence: enable the Write MCP tools option in your organization's System Preferences

XB15.name: Fusion flow into Journey Optimizer
XB15.src: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer modules (Workfront Fusion)
XB15.scope: Set up the Journey Optimizer connection in Fusion (Developer Console credentials, organization, sandbox) and build the scenario that creates content templates or fragments when Workfront work is approved.
XB15.evidence: allow you to create, read, update, or delete records

XC01.name: Connect Sites to the DAM with OpenAPI
XC01.src: Experience League: Integrate remote AEM Assets with AEM Sites
XC01.scope: Set the asset delivery repository and IMS client variables in Cloud Manager, configure the Image v3 component and HTTPS, and confirm authors can pick remote assets.
XC01.evidence: Set up the following environment variables for AEM as a Cloud Service

XC02.name: Image modifiers, and smart crops where licensed, for pages
XC02.src: Experience League: Dynamic Media with OpenAPI capabilities
XC02.scope: Set up the image modifiers, and smart crops where the client's Dynamic Media edition includes them, for the Image v3 and Teaser v2 components (other components need custom work), so each placement gets the right size and format from the DAM.
XC02.evidence: on-the-fly image transformation using URL parameters known as image modifiers

XC03.name: AEM Assets repository in Journey Optimizer
XC03.src: Experience League: Use Assets in Journey Optimizer
XC03.scope: Add marketers to the Assets Cloud Services product profiles, select the Assets as a Cloud Service repository in Journey Optimizer, and set up campaign asset folders.
XC03.evidence: Before using Adobe Experience Manager Assets as a Cloud Service, you must add users to Assets Cloud Services.

XC04.name: Dynamic Media renditions in journey content
XC04.src: Experience League: Combine solutions and apps to manage your content
XC04.scope: For clients with Dynamic Media, set up the approved renditions and image parameters marketers pick in the asset selector (Content Advisor where it has rolled out), so journey content always uses the latest version.
XC04.evidence: Dynamic media allowing you to seamlessly select and use approved dynamic media renditions within Journey Optimizer

XC05.name: Content Fragments for Journey Optimizer
XC05.scope: Allow the Content Fragment API in the Dispatcher, create the ajo-enabled tag for each sandbox, model channel-ready fragments, and publish them for campaigns and journeys.
XC05.evidence: Content Fragments must be tagged with the Journey Optimizer-specific tag (ajo-enabled:{OrgId}/{SandboxName}).

XC06.name: Personalized fragments and variations
XC06.scope: Add placeholders to fragment text and map them to profile or contextual attributes in Journey Optimizer, and set up fragment variations for audiences or channels.
XC06.evidence: To enable real-time personalization, all placeholders used within a Content fragment must be explicitly declared by the user as parameters

XC07.name: AJO references and previews in AEM
XC07.src: Experience League: Using the Content Fragments AJO External References Extension
XC07.scope: Enable the AJO External References extension so authors see and preview the campaigns, journeys and templates that use a fragment before they change it.
XC07.evidence: fetching references to Content Fragment from all organizations and sandboxes associated with predefined tags

XC10.name: Connect AEM Sites to Commerce with CIF
XC10.src: Experience League: Getting started with AEM Commerce as a Cloud Service
XC10.scope: Once Adobe provisions the CIF add-on, set the COMMERCE_ENDPOINT variable for each environment in Cloud Manager and the CIF configuration for store view and catalog root.
XC10.evidence: you must provide the GraphQL endpoint URL by way of a Cloud Manager environment variable. The variable name is COMMERCE_ENDPOINT.

XC11.name: Product-enriched content experiences
XC11.scope: Build the commerce-specific content (product teasers, category and campaign content, Content Fragments) that authors assemble from products they search and browse in AEM, using Content Fragments and headless content for new builds rather than CIF Core Components, which Adobe has put in maintenance mode.
XC11.evidence: a seamless integration of your product data into AEM (Search, browse, and find products within the AEM UI)

XC12.name: CIF to Edge Delivery transition plan
XC12.scope: For existing CIF storefronts, plan a phased move to Edge Delivery with Commerce drop-in components, running Edge Delivery and CIF pages side by side.
XC12.evidence: start by moving only a subset of pages to Edge Delivery and running Edge Delivery and CIF pages

XC13.name: Set up AEM Assets for Commerce metadata
XC13.src: Experience League: Configure the AEM Assets Project
XC13.scope: Enable the Commerce integration in Cloud Manager (or install the assets-commerce package on older releases), activate Dynamic Media with OpenAPI, and set the approval metadata schema.
XC13.evidence: enable the integration in Cloud Manager by setting an environment variable and activating Dynamic Media with OpenAPI capabilities

XC14.name: Connect Commerce and set SKU matching
XC14.scope: Set IMS permissions and the AEM Assets Integration settings in the Commerce Admin, choose Match by product SKU, set the Visualization Owner and start the first sync.
XC14.evidence: matches the SKU in the asset metadata with the Commerce product SKU

XC15.name: Migrate Commerce media to AEM Assets
XC15.src: Experience League: Migrate media files to AEM
XC15.scope: Move existing product and category media from Commerce into AEM Assets, tag SKUs, roles and positions, and approve, keeping Commerce as Visualization Owner until the sync completes.
XC15.evidence: provide built-in features to streamline media file migration from Commerce to the AEM Assets digital asset management system

XC16.name: Custom asset matching with App Builder
XC16.scope: Where SKU matching is not enough, build custom matching logic in Adobe Developer App Builder that maps assets to products.
XC16.evidence: Implementing custom matching requires developing custom code in Adobe Developer App Builder to define how assets are matched with products.
